items.title: Weak topology on a normed space
items.statement: For a real or complex normed space X, sigma(X,X*) is the initial topology induced by its bounded scalar-linear functionals.
items.strategy: Use scalar-linear duals throughout; convexity is real convexity and separation uses real parts in the complex case.

items.title: Basic weak neighborhoods
items.statement: At x, sets defined by finitely many inequalities |f_j(y-x)|<epsilon, with epsilon>0 and f_j in X*, form a weak neighborhood base.
items.strategy: Intersect finitely many inverse images of scalar open disks; shrink their radii to one positive minimum. Show vector addition and scalar multiplication are continuous and these neighborhoods are convex and balanced at zero.

items.title: Weak topology is hausdorff
items.statement: The weak topology of a real or complex normed space is Hausdorff.
items.strategy: For x!=y choose a bounded functional separating them and disjoint scalar disks. HB is the intended relative principle; the published separation supplier inherits AC, recorded as a blocker in notes.

items.title: Weak convergence of nets and sequences
items.statement: A net x_i converges weakly to x when f(x_i) tends to f(x) for every f in X*. Sequences are the special case indexed by the natural numbers.
items.strategy: Finite simultaneous eventual conditions are exactly the neighborhood definition of convergence. Closure is topological, never defined by sequences.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Basic weak star neighborhoods
items.statement: At f in X*, finite inequalities |(g-f)(x_j)|<epsilon form a weak-star neighborhood base.
items.strategy: Use the predecessor initial topology on evaluations. Evaluations distinguish distinct functionals, so this topology is Hausdorff in ZF without norming HB. Verify vector operations and local convexity directly.

Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Weak star convergence
items.statement: A net f_i in X* converges weak-star to f in X* exactly when f_i(x) tends to f(x) for every x in X.
items.strategy: The specified limit must belong to X*: pointwise limits of bounded functionals on an incomplete space need not be bounded.

Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Continuous dual of a weak topology
items.statement: The scalar-linear continuous dual of (X,sigma(X,X*)) is X*.
items.strategy: Continuity at zero bounds a functional on a finite-coordinate neighborhood. Scaling proves it vanishes on the common kernel; factor through the image in the finite-dimensional coordinate space, extend there using a finite basis, and express it as a finite linear combination of the original functionals. No algebraic-dual identification.

items.title: Continuous dual of a weak star topology
items.statement: Every weak-star continuous scalar-linear functional on X* is f -> f(x) for a unique x in X.
items.strategy: Factor through finitely many evaluations using their common kernel and finite-dimensional extension. Their linear combination is evaluation at a single vector. Existence is ZF; uniqueness uses dual separation and inherits its supplier cost.

items.title: Norm closed convex iff weakly closed
items.statement: A convex subset of a normed space is norm closed iff it is weakly closed. More generally its norm and weak closures agree.
items.strategy: Apply the earlier Mazur separation theorem, with real parts of complex-linear functionals; weak-open sets are norm open.

items.title: Weak closure of the unit sphere is the closed unit ball
items.statement: In an infinite-dimensional normed space, the weak closure of the norm unit sphere is the closed unit ball.
items.strategy: Given x of norm<1 and finitely many tests, choose a nonzero vector in their common kernel using finite-dimensional rank. Along its real line through x the norm crosses 1 by continuity. The reverse inclusion follows from weak closedness of the ball. The kernel/rank and intermediate-value suppliers remain to be individually audited.

items.title: Weakly convergent sequences are norm bounded
items.statement: Assuming the norming Hahn–Banach principle and countable choice, every weakly convergent sequence in a normed space is norm bounded; if X is Banach, every weak-star convergent sequence in X* is norm bounded.
items.strategy: Apply sequential uniform boundedness to J_X(x_n) on the Banach space X*, then use the bidual isometry. For weak-star sequences apply it on X. BLOCKED: the requested countable-choice supplier is missing; the published Sokal theorem explicitly also assumes DC and cannot replace it.

items.title: Weak convergence implies lower semicontinuity of the norm
items.statement: For a weakly convergent net x_i -> x, ||x|| <= liminf_i ||x_i|| (extended-real net liminf).
items.strategy: For each unit-dual f, |f(x)|=lim |f(x_i)| <= liminf ||x_i||; take the supremum. Equivalently all closed norm balls are weakly closed, avoiding a separate net-liminf convention if needed. No boundedness of the net is asserted.

items.title: Weak and norm topologies agree iff finite dimensional
items.statement: The weak and norm topologies agree exactly when X is finite dimensional.
items.strategy: Coordinate functionals in finite dimension give the norm topology. In infinite dimension every finite family has a nonzero common kernel, so every weak neighborhood of zero is norm unbounded.

items.title: Infinite dimensional weak topology is not first countable
items.statement: Under countable choice and the norming/separation hypotheses, an infinite-dimensional normed space has no countable weak local base at zero.
items.strategy: Refine a supplied countable base by finite-coordinate basic neighborhoods using AC_omega. The union of the finite lists is countable after the same choice. Finite-coordinate factorization puts X* in their algebraic span. Greedy extraction from the enumeration gives a finite or countably infinite Hamel basis. X* is Banach; the latter is excluded by the earlier no-countable-Hamel theorem. Finite-dimensional X* and separation force finite-dimensional X. Audit the actual inherited choice costs before certifying the intended bound.

items.title: Annihilators are weak and weak star closed
items.statement: For M subset X and N subset X*, M-perp is weak-star closed and preannihilator N is weakly closed. For linear subspaces the earlier bipolar identities apply.
items.strategy: Intersect the appropriate evaluation kernels. Cite the published bipolar theorem at its original home; do not duplicate or rehome it.

items.title: Transpose is weak to weak continuous
items.statement: A bounded T:X->Y is weak-to-weak continuous; its transpose T*:Y*->X* is continuous for the weak topologies sigma(Y*,Y**) and sigma(X*,X**).
items.strategy: For T compose each y* with T. Apply the same reasoning to the bounded operator T*, testing by X**.

items.title: Transpose is weak star to weak star continuous
items.statement: A bounded T:X->Y has weak-star continuous transpose T*:Y*->X*. Conversely a bounded weak-star continuous scalar-linear S:Y*->X* has a unique bounded preadjoint T:X->Y with S=T*.
items.strategy: For each x, f -> (Sf)(x) is evaluation at a unique Tx. Uniqueness proves linearity; ||Tx||=sup_{||f||<=1}|(Sf)(x)|<=||S||||x|| proves boundedness. Forward continuity is direct evaluation. Do not require reflexivity or completeness.

items.title: Strong and weak operator topologies
items.statement: On B(X,Y), SOT is initial for T->Tx with Y norm topology; WOT is initial for T->f(Tx), x in X, f in Y*.
items.strategy: Specify nets: strong convergence means ||T_i x-Tx||->0 for each x; weak operator convergence means f(T_i x)->f(Tx) for each x,f.

items.title: Norm implies strong implies weak operator convergence
items.statement: For nets of bounded operators, norm convergence implies SOT convergence, which implies WOT convergence.
items.strategy: Use ||(T_i-T)x||<=||T_i-T||||x|| and |f((T_i-T)x)|<=||f||||(T_i-T)x||. No assertion that reverse implications hold.

items.title: Coordinate vectors converge weakly to zero in ell p
items.statement: In real or complex ell^p, 1<p<infinity, e_n tends weakly to zero while ||e_n||=1.
items.strategy: For real scalars use the published counting-measure duality. For complex scalars, restrict Re F and Im F to real ell^p, represent each by real ell^q sequences, and reconstruct F by complex linearity. Each representing coordinate tends to zero. This finite realification argument must be written inline; the real supplier alone does not prove the complex claim.

items.title: Coordinate vectors do not converge weakly to zero in ell one
items.statement: In real or complex ell^1 the coordinate vectors do not converge weakly to zero.
items.strategy: The summation functional has value 1 at every e_n; its norm is 1 by the absolute-sum estimate. Coordinate tests force any weak limit to be zero, so there is no weak limit.

items.title: Coordinate evaluations converge weak star to zero in ell one star
items.statement: The coordinate functionals e_n in ell^infinity=(ell^1)* converge weak-star to zero and all have norm 1.
items.strategy: Every absolutely summable x has x_n->0; these are exactly the weak-star evaluations.

items.title: Weak star and weak topologies on a dual can differ
items.statement: On ell^1=(c0)*, weak-star and weak topologies differ.
items.strategy: e_n is weak-star null since every x in c0 has x_n->0. The bounded summation functional on ell^1 equals 1 on e_n, so the sequence is not weakly null.

items.title: Weak closure can exceed sequential weak closure
items.statement: In real ell^2 the set A={sqrt(n)e_n:n>=1} is sequentially weakly closed, but zero belongs to its weak closure and not to A.
items.strategy: BS Exercise 3.60: if finitely many ell^2 tests exclude every sqrt(n)e_n from a basic zero-neighborhood, then sum_j |y_j(n)|^2 >= epsilon^2/n for every n, contradicting summability. Any weakly convergent sequence in A is norm bounded, hence has finite range and its limit belongs to that finite closed set. Harmonic divergence and ell^2 duality exact suppliers still need closure review.

items.title: Right shift powers converge in wot not sot
items.statement: On real or complex ell^2 the powers R^n of the unilateral right shift converge in WOT to zero but not in SOT.
items.strategy: Represent real functionals by ell^2 and obtain complex representation by restricting real and imaginary parts to real sequences, then reconstructing by complex linearity. Tail Cauchy–Schwarz bounds each pairing with R^n x by ||x|| times an ell^2 tail norm. R^n is an isometry, excluding strong convergence. Realification is an inline obligation, not an appeal to a nonexistent complex version of the published theorem.

items.title: Left shift powers converge in sot not operator norm
items.statement: On ell^2 the powers L^n of the unilateral left shift converge in SOT to zero but ||L^n||=1.
items.strategy: The squared norm is the tail sum of |x_k|^2. The moving witness e_(n+1) proves the lower operator norm bound. No Hilbert adjoint theorem is used.

items.title: Pointwise boundedness without a uniform bound on an incomplete domain
items.statement: On c00 with the supremum norm, T_n(x)=n x_n is pointwise eventually zero, but ||T_n||=n. The domain is incomplete.
items.strategy: Finite support gives eventual zero, and e_n attains the norm bound. Finite truncations of (1/k) are Cauchy in the supremum norm and their only possible coordinatewise limit is not in c00. Reprove directly rather than using a foreign B item as a dependency.

items.title: A weakly convergent net need not be eventually norm bounded
items.statement: Every infinite-dimensional normed space has a weakly null net whose norms tend to infinity.
items.strategy: Index by all triples (U,n,x) with U a weak zero-neighborhood, n a positive integer, x in U and ||x||>=n. Order by reverse inclusion of U and increasing n; ties give a directed preorder. Nonempty finite intersections are unbounded by the kernel argument. The net is the carried point x. This avoids choosing a point for every neighborhood globally; it is not eventually norm bounded.

items.title: Dual ball as a closed subset of a product
items.statement: Evaluation embeds the closed dual unit ball of a real or complex normed X homeomorphically as a closed subset of the product of scalar disks D_x={z:|z|<=||x||}.
items.strategy: The subspace product topology is weak-star. Additivity and scalar homogeneity are closed equations; the coordinate bounds imply boundedness and norm<=1. All equations together characterize the image. Treat X={0} as well. Compactness of finite-dimensional scalar disks must use an earlier local result.

items.statement: Assuming BPI (the ultrafilter lemma), the closed dual unit ball of every normed space is compact for sigma(X*,X).
items.strategy: Use compact Hausdorff scalar factors, compact-Hausdorff Tychonoff, and the closed image lemma. X need not be Banach. BPI is the intended sufficient cost; audit the complete inherited Tychonoff proof before claiming an exact implemented cost.

items.title: Weak star compactness of polar sets
items.statement: If U is a norm neighborhood of zero in X, its absolute polar U^circ={f in X*: |f(u)|<=1 for every u in U} is weak-star compact under BPI.
items.strategy: Define the absolute polar explicitly before its use. Since U contains rB_X for some r>0, its polar lies in r^(-1)B_X*. It is an intersection of closed evaluation constraints. Scaling the dual ball and closed-subspace compactness give the result; U need not be convex or balanced.

items.title: Dual ball weak star metrizable for separable predual
items.statement: Given a fixed dense sequence (x_n) in a normed X, on each norm-bounded subset of X* the weak-star topology is induced by d(f,g)=sum_(n>=1) 2^(-n) min(1,|(f-g)(x_n)|).
items.strategy: Dense evaluations separate by the common norm bound. Control the series tail and finitely many evaluations in one direction; approximate finitely many arbitrary test vectors by the supplied dense sequence in the other. The boundedness restriction is essential; a metric on the whole dual is not claimed.

items.title: Separable banach dual ball is weak star sequentially compact
items.statement: Under BPI, every sequence in the closed dual unit ball of a separable Banach space has a weak-star convergent subsequence.

items.title: Goldstine
items.statement: For a normed X, J_X(B_X) is weak-star dense in B_(X**).
items.strategy: Given x** in the bidual ball, map B_X into scalar m-space by f_1,...,f_m. If its convex closure misses the vector of x** values, separate that point from the closed convex set in finite dimension. A real separating functional is Re of a scalar-linear combination f of the f_j; get Re x**(f)>sup_BX Re f=||f||, contradicting ||x**||<=1. No compactness theorem. Intended relative HB cost is blocked by the stronger AC hypothesis on the published HB chain.

items.title: Banach dieudonne linear subspace criterion
items.statement: For a real or complex Banach X and a linear subspace E of X*, E is weak-star closed iff E intersect B_(X*) is weak-star closed.
items.strategy: Follow BS Theorem 3.40 and Corollary 3.41, pp138–141. Scaling gives closedness of all bounded slices and then norm closedness. For f0 outside E use compact FIP on bounded slices to choose successive finite tests S_n in B_X; recursive refinements use DC. Block-enumerate the union of n^(-1)S_n as a norm-null sequence x_i. Its map T:X*->c0 separates T(f0) from T(E); HB and c0*=ell1 produce coefficients a_i with x0=sum a_i x_i in X, vanishing on E but not on f0. Prove all recursive estimates and the separating image-neighborhood assertion, not just the final series. Intended BPI+DC+HB; supplier HB currently inherits AC. Full local support inventory/closure is still blocked.

items.title: Extreme point and face
items.statement: For a real convex set K in a real or complex vector space, x is extreme if x=ty+(1-t)z, y,z in K, 0<t<1 implies y=z=x. A face F is a nonempty convex subset of K satisfying the analogous endpoint property.
items.strategy: Distinguish arbitrary faces from exposed faces and from extremal subsets, which need not be convex. Use the missing LCS prerequisite pair to establish the ambient topology before the compact theorems.

items.statement: A real-valued continuous affine functional on a nonempty compact convex K attains its minimum; the minimizers form a nonempty compact face. Faces of faces are faces.
items.strategy: Scalar compactness gives attainment. Affinity proves the endpoint property, continuity closedness, and convexity follows from equality at the minimum. Verify transitivity directly.

items.title: Krein milman existence of extreme points
items.statement: Under AC, every nonempty compact convex subset K of a locally convex Hausdorff topological vector space has an extreme point.
items.strategy: Order nonempty compact faces by reverse inclusion. Chain intersections are nonempty by compact FIP and are faces. Zorn supplies a minimal face. If it has two points, a continuous real separating functional has a proper nonempty minimizing face, a contradiction. items.title: Krein milman closed convex hull form
items.statement: Under AC, a compact convex subset K of a locally convex Hausdorff space is the closed convex hull of its extreme points; allow empty K with empty hull.
items.strategy: For nonempty K, separate any point outside the closed convex hull of ext(K) from that hull by a continuous real functional. Its maximizing face in K has an extreme point by existence, which is extreme in K by transitivity, contradicting separation. The hull is closed inside compact K.

items.title: Bauer maximum principle
items.statement: Under AC, a real-valued upper-semicontinuous convex function on a nonempty compact convex subset K of a locally convex Hausdorff space attains its maximum at an extreme point of K.
items.strategy: Use the compact nonempty maximum set M. Convexity makes M extremal but not necessarily convex: x^2 on [-1,1] has M={-1,1}. Order nonempty compact extremal subsets of M by reverse inclusion; intersections are extremal and compact. A separating functional on a nonsingleton minimal subset cuts a proper compact extremal subset by maximizing; therefore it is a singleton extreme in K. This is the standard proof in Ball pp1–2, not an invalid invocation of KM on M. Inline extremal-subset definition and its transitivity are required.

items.title: Milman converse for compact generating sets
items.statement: If K is compact convex in a locally convex Hausdorff space, A subset K, and K=closed convex hull(A), then ext(K) subset closure(A). In particular a compact generating A contains ext(K).
items.strategy: Hanche-Olsen Theorem 22 pp13–14. For extreme w outside closure(A), choose a convex zero-neighborhood U with (w+U-U) disjoint from closure(A). Cover compact closure(A) by finitely many x_j+U. Let K_j be closed convex hull((x_j+U) intersect closure(A)); these lie in K and avoid w since their preclosures avoid the open w+U. The convex hull of the finite union K_j is compact via the simplex times their finite product and equals K. A finite convex representation of extreme w forces every positive-weight point to equal w, contradicting avoidance. Do not claim closure(co(A)) compact for arbitrary compact A without the assumed compact K.

items.statement: For compact Hausdorff K, regular Borel probability measures form a compact subset of C(K)* for convergence against continuous functions, under BPI plus the representation suppliers.

items.statement: For compact Hausdorff K, the extreme regular Borel probability measures are exactly the Dirac masses.

A zero-one regular probability has nonempty support by compactness and regularity, and cannot have two support points with disjoint neighborhoods; hence is Dirac. Dirac masses are extreme by positivity outside their singleton. Verify regularity of restrictions and the support assertion from exact earlier measure results before approval.

items.title: Weak star compact does not imply weak star sequentially compact
items.statement: The weak-star compact unit ball of (ell^infinity)* need not be sequentially compact.
items.strategy: The norm-one coordinate evaluations Lambda_n(x)=x_n lie in it. For any subsequence with increasing indices n_k, prescribe x_(n_k)=(-1)^k and x_j=0 otherwise. This x in ell^infinity makes the evaluated subsequence divergent. Hence no subsequence is weak-star convergent. Compactness uses BPI; the obstruction is explicit.

items.title: Banach alaoglu versus sequential alaoglu
items.statement: Alaoglu compactness, separable bounded-ball metrizability, and sequential compactness have distinct hypotheses and proof costs.
